tips: Start with 1 teaspoon of clay per pound (454 g) of soaping oils; Lovely Greens' example clay bars are all made at exactly this rate, and 1-2 tsp per pound is the usual working range for French green clay.

Add clay as a slurry, not a dry powder: pre-mix it with three times its volume of distilled water (five times for smectite clays) before adding at trace. This extra water stops the clay from clumping, accelerating trace, or cracking the finished bars, and many soapmakers hydrate the slurry several hours ahead so it turns smooth and fluid.

Clay is one of the most stable natural soap colorants: its colors survive saponification and don't fade or morph during cure the way plant-based colorants do, so a French green clay bar keeps its sage-green color long-term.

Leaf-based green powders (spirulina, nettle, matcha, spinach and similar) fade toward yellow in ordinary daylight; cure and store those bars in the dark to slow the fade. For a natural green that actually lasts, Lovely Greens recommends alfalfa powder, or lean on the mineral stability of French green clay.
